content:
The image shows young corn plants with prominent **pale yellow/white parallel stripes** running lengthwise along the leaves, alternating with green tissue. The leaves appear somewhat erect and narrow. Multiple plants exhibit this pattern.

Key observations:
- Broad, parallel light-colored stripes alternating with green tissue (not mosaic, not spots)
- Stripes run from base toward tip of leaf
- Leaves look somewhat narrower and more upright than normal
- No pustules, no spots, no galls — purely a striping/chlorosis pattern

Matching against candidates:
- **Downy mildew**: "new leaves emerge with white parallel stripes of varying width alternating with green tissue" — matches very closely
- **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus**: would show mosaic patches, short streaks, irregular mottle — not matching
- **Maize_streak_virus**: typically narrow, broken yellow streaks — stripes here are broader and more uniform
- **Stewarts_wilt**: pale green/yellow streaks from flea beetle feeding scars, wavy margins — different pattern

The broad parallel white-to-yellow stripes alternating with green tissue, on erect narrowed leaves, is the hallmark of Downy mildew in corn.
